title: Trading Psychology
promise: Your biggest opponent in the market isn’t a hedge fund. It’s the person staring back from your screen.
unlock: Spot fear and greed in your own trades
Stop a bad day before tilt makes it worse
Let a hot move go instead of chasing it
Take a small loss on purpose, before hope makes it big
Keep a trading journal and find one pattern a week

questions.q: You win 7 of 10 trades. Your wins average $40, your losses $120. Are you making money?
options: Yes: 7 of 10 is a great win rate
No: you’re down $80 overall
You’re breaking even
questions.why: A high win rate can still lose money. Each loss is three times a win, so three losses wipe out all seven wins and more.

questions.q: Two $100 losses this morning hit your $200 daily limit. You feel you must win it back before lunch. What do you do?
options: One more trade at double size
One more trade at normal size
Stop for the day, as your rule says
questions.why: Most people feel that urge. Doubling up to win it back is revenge trading, and your limit exists for exactly this moment.
questions.work: Down $200. One doubled loss adds $200 more. That’s $400 lost, twice your limit.
questions.added: New situation written for the Academy

questions.q: A stock you don’t follow is up 40% this week and all over your feed. You have no plan for it. What’s the disciplined move?
options: Buy a little, just in case
Let it go: no setup, no trade
Buy now, make a plan later
questions.why: A move you didn’t plan, where FOMO is loudest. With no setup there’s no entry and no stop. Another setup always comes.

questions.q: You’re down 20% on a stock. You tell yourself you’ll sell “once it’s back to even”. Which bias is this?
options: FOMO
Loss aversion
Revenge trading
questions.why: Waiting for “even” dodges the pain of making the loss real. But the loss is already real. Ask: would I buy this today, at this price?
questions.added: New situation written for the Academy

questions.q: Your journal shows 6 trades marked “bored”. 5 of them lost. What should your weekly review lead to?
options: Nothing: it’s just bad luck
A rule: no trades when you’re bored
Trade bigger when bored to stay sharp
questions.why: 5 of 6 is a pattern, not luck. The weekly review turns one losing pattern into one rule.

retry.q: You win 8 of 10 trades at +$25 each. Your 2 losses are −$150 each. Where do you stand?
options: Up $200: 8 wins is a lot
Breaking even
Down $100 overall
retry.why: Count the size, not just the wins. Two big losses wipe out eight small wins and more.

retry.q: Your rule: stop after 2 losses a day. You’ve had 2, you’re angry, and the market is open for 3 more hours. What do you do?
options: Close the app until tomorrow
Trade faster to catch up
Double your size on the next setup
retry.why: Anger makes bad setups look good. The rule holds on the days it hurts: tomorrow is a new day.
retry.added: New situation written for the Academy

retry.q: A coin jumps 30% in a day and your group chat is buzzing. Your plan has no entry for it. What do you do?
options: Buy now before it runs further
Buy now and set a stop later
Skip it: no setup, no trade
retry.why: The chat is noise, not a setup. Buying after a spike means buying high with no clear stop. Another setup always comes.
retry.added: New situation written for the Academy

retry.q: You bought at $20 with a stop at $18. Price hits $18 and you feel sure it will bounce. What does your plan say?
options: Take the planned loss
Move the stop to $16
Buy more at $18 to lower your average
retry.why: The stop decides, not hope. Moving it or adding to a loser makes the loss bigger than you planned.
retry.work: $20 − $18 = $2 a share: the loss you planned before the trade.
retry.added: New situation written for the Academy

retry.q: Your journal shows your 4 biggest losses all came the day after a big win, marked “confident”. What should your review lead to?
options: Nothing: big wins mean you’re good
A rule: normal size the day after a big win
Stop keeping a journal
retry.why: Four of four is a pattern. Turn it into one rule, then check next week whether it helped.

refresher.title: Lesson 1 · Fear and greed in your own head
refresher.text: Winning often isn’t the same as making money. Fear closes winners early and hope lets losers run. Set the stop and target before you enter, then follow them.

refresher.title: Lesson 2 · Revenge trading and tilt
refresher.text: Hit your daily limit? You’re done for the day. After a loss, trade the same size or smaller, never bigger.

refresher.title: Lesson 3 · FOMO and chasing
refresher.text: FOMO makes you buy after the move, near the top, with no clear stop. Write your setup down and enter only when it shows. No setup, no trade.

refresher.title: Lesson 4 · Loss aversion: why you hold losers
refresher.text: A loss hurts about twice as much as an equal gain feels good, so you’re tempted to hold losers. The loss is real before you sell. The stop decides, not hope.

refresher.title: Lesson 5 · Your trading journal
refresher.text: Log setup, entry, stop, target, result and emotion. Each week, turn one losing pattern into a rule. 5 of 6 “bored” trades lost? No trading when bored.
